To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method for calculating the propagation of light in multilayer dielectric waveguides, which can be used to design self-filtering waveguides for use in integrated optics applications.
the energy characteristics of the normal modes of multilayer dielectric waveguides are calculated and the possibility of self-filtering is shown.
we have obtained expressions for the energy characteristics of the normal modes of a multilayer dielectric waveguide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of optical waveguides, in which light is guided along a planar or curved surface.
the propagation of optical waves along the interface between two media with different dielectric constants.
a study of the propagation of optical waves in layered dielectric waveguides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy characteristics of a layered waveguide are strongly dependent on the layer parameters.
the energy characteristics of the waveguide modes have been studied in great detail, and that the results of this work are applicable to many types of waveguides.
the energy characteristics of the waveguide modes are strongly influenced by the waveguide layer structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the normal modes of the layered dielectric waveguides have the following properties: (1) the longitudinal energy flux of the mode is directed toward the waveguide axis; (2) the power in the waveguide layers decreases with distance from the axis; (3) the attenuation coefficient of a mode increases with the distance from the axis.
the energy characteristics of the normal modes are determined by the waveguide structure.
the theory of the normal modes of a waveguide of any shape and with an arbitrary number of layers can be constructed on a rigorous basis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy characteristics of the normal modes are very sensitive to variations in waveguide parameters.
, in a self-filtering structure, the energy of the fundamental mode propagating in the cladding is concentrated in a narrow layer adjacent to the waveguide surface.
the energy characteristics of the normal modes are determined primarily by the ratio of the refractive indices and thickness of the layers.
